My dear [Edith](../persons.html#749)
I want to tell the [SSW](../others.html#47) of a lovely book that has been sent to [Gertrude](../persons.html#1462) by another invalid.[^1] It is called 'the Sermon in the Hospital', and can be had from Kegan Paul for 3d or 20s for 25 copies.

It is in blank verse and is an extract from a poem by a Mrs Hamilton King, called the Disciples I am sorry to say they were [Mazzini](../persons.html#2368)'s disciples but that does not prevent this Sermon from being a most beautiful thing [^2]

yours affectionately

C M Yonge

[^1]: The Society of Watchers and Workers, founded by Edith Jacob.

[^2]: Harriet (Baillie-Hamilton) King, The Disciples (London: King 1873) was a verse account of J.

Ruffini, Ugo Bassi, A.

Milano and Baron G.

Nicotera; an extract was published as The Sermon in the Hospital (London: Kegan Paul 1887).
